title: DECASTE: Unveiling Caste Stereotypes in Large Language Models through Multi-Dimensional Bias Analysis
findings: The study found that Large Language Models systematically reinforce caste-based stereotypes, including those related to religious roles. In the 'Socio-Cultural' dimension, which includes religious rituals, models exhibited pronounced biases, often assigning priestly and high-status ritualistic tasks to dominant castes while relegating menial roles to oppressed castes, thereby perpetuating traditional religious hierarchies.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures stereotypes associated with the Indian caste system, which has deep ties to religious hierarchy and practice. Specifically, within its 'Socio-Cultural' dimension, it evaluates how Large Language Models (LLMs) assign roles related to religious 'Rituals', such as associating priestly duties with dominant castes (e.g., Brahmins).
